minutes.headline: Select Board heard renewed criticism of the school building committee and changed the MART van route.
minutes.summary: Public comment again carried a letter criticizing the school building committee's use of contingency funds, and board members argued over whether it belonged there. The board proclaimed Boys and Girls Club Week, took up the MART route change, and moved on a third amendment to the regional hazardous waste agreement. The town manager described plans to lease the TCP building to cover its carrying costs, and the meeting ended with a motion to adjourn.

public_comment.topic: Email read to the board criticizing the school building committee's use of contingency funds for discretionary items and lack of objective standards.
Reminder that the septic sewer loan program is accepting applications, at two percent interest set up as a betterment.
Asked whether a handicapped veteran could be picked up at his trailer under the changed MART route; thanked the senior center.

Change the MART routes as explained by the town manager
Approve the third amendment to the inter-municipal agreement for the household hazardous waste program, adding Stow

budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the committee is considering spending a sum large relative to the town budget, while another said many items were removed and the project is under budget.
A member noted the committee had limited funds this year and debated a small police vehicle purchase.
Fare for seniors and disabled riders was stated, with transfers available.
Adding Stow carries no additional cost to member towns; the program runs a small surplus held for capital improvements.
An accounts payable warrant total was read.
figures_as_heard: six hundred and forty-four thousand two hundred and nineteen dollars and ninety two cents

budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee renewed regular and special education transportation contracts; the regular contract rises because of a state sick-time mandate and the special needs contract is flat.
Projects carry a stipend for about a hundred hours of work.
There is no room in the current budget, though it may be found there; appropriate approvals would be needed.
Neither the school FY17 budget nor the town covers carrying costs, so the town manager plans leases to tenants that cover costs fully.
Loans are written at a set interest rate and set up as a betterment.

decisions.decision: Discussion of the management plan moved to the March 15 agenda.
Adding an alternate member to the stormwater task force will be put on a coming agenda with a broader discussion of committee alternates.
Town manager to look into a construction-style trash bag.
Next week's agenda will include a broad discussion of the board's role as liaison and member on committees.

what_happened.line: The board took up a change to the MART van routes as explained by the town manager; the minutes do not record an audible outcome.
A motion was made on a third amendment to the household hazardous waste agreement adding Stow, which the minutes say carries no added cost to member towns; the outcome was not audible.
The board heard a letter criticizing the school building committee's use of contingency funds, and members then disagreed over whether it belonged in public comment.
The town manager said neither the school budget nor the town covers carrying costs of the TCP building, and plans leases to tenants that cover those costs.
The board signed and read a Boys and Girls Club Week proclamation, and set a broader discussion of its committee roles for next week's agenda.

why_it_matters: Whether the TCP building's carrying costs fall on the town budget, mostly taxes, or on tenants depends on leases the town manager plans, so residents may see the building's cost handled through rents rather than the tax bill.
The school building committee's contingency spending is a live dispute, and the members' differing views on it bear on how a school project is overseen and what it ends up costing.
